observations: pixel_ring contains a ring-like 10-column pixel pattern centered at 24,24.
pixel_south is a short diagonal pixel sequence centered at 30,42.
score_416 names 416 and sets tempo to 84; it includes Ab4.
sound_416 contains a 416 Hz note among its frequencies.
vector_416 depicts two horizontal lines and labels 416 km/s and Ab4 415.3.

INPUT.json defines directed connections from pixel_ring to sound_ring and pixel_south, from color_416 to vector_416, from score_416 to sound_416, from sound_416 to field_416, from sound_ring to sound_416, and from couplet_ring_refusal to pixel_ring.
interpretation: I made a self-contained SVG that turns the ring motif into a broken angular orbit, lets the southward pixel diagonal continue beyond the ring, and places two nearly coincident horizontal tones beside it. The final offset is kept visible rather than resolved. The artifact combines geometry, color, and the small difference between the score's Ab4 label and the 416 Hz signal.
new_relation_or_transformation: The pixel_south diagonal is extended into a long descending path from the ring and visually paired with the two near-parallel tone lines; the difference is represented as an unresolved offset.
possible_dependence_on_input: With no explicit graph, I might have treated the ring, southern pixels, color, and tone mismatch as separate items rather than composing them into one spatial progression. Another graph could foreground a different pair or sequence. Asset-internal text already suggests some of these associations, so the graph is not the only possible source of the composition.
limitations: This is one interpretive visual transformation, not evidence of emergence or causation. The supplied assets themselves contain semantic cues and path references. The SVG is static and does not render audio.
